This week, #WashAndSet reflects a continued interest in professional salon services on TikTok, where hair is washed, conditioned, and set on rollers before drying to create smooth, polished, and long-lasting results. #CherryAngioma signals the growing consumer attention toward skin education and concerns, as users seek information around specific skin conditions. The #LashExpert hashtag points to demand for specialized beauty professionals who showcase precision techniques and lash transformations, while #MakeupWithSPF captures the rising interest in hybrid beauty products that combine cosmetic performance with everyday sun protection. #StylistHair signals engagement with hairstylist-driven content that blends transformations and recommendations from experts. These trends reveal that beauty consumers are increasingly drawn to content centered on expert guidance, visible results, and multifunctional routines.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a growing interest in more personalized and occasion-driven fragrance choices. The search for masculine fragrance suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Indie perfume highlights a shift toward niche artistry and unique scents. Birthday cake perfume points to playful, gourmand fragrances inspired by dessert-like notes. Bridal perfume underscores the role of scent in key life moments, with consumers seeking signature fragrances for special occasions. Meanwhile, clean fresh perfume indicates that consumers continue to seek out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to richer, gourmand scents.

Arabiyat Prestige and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect a growing interest in heritage-led scents defined by richness, high concentration, and long-lasting wear. YCZ signals the rise of social media-driven accessibility, where viral scents and dupes offer more affordable alternatives to traditional designer perfumes. Tenth Muse reflects interest in solid perfumes that prioritize portability, skin sensitivity, and easy application. Sorce underscores interest in bold, imaginative fragrances that lean into gourmand and whimsical scent profiles inspired by fantasy and more playful notes.

Recent findings suggest that on TikTok, #PrismHair reflects an interest in bold, color-driven hair looks that emphasize a multi-tonal, iridescent finish. #NaturalNailJourney highlights a shift toward nail health and growth, as consumers document and prioritize stronger, natural nails. #KeratinOil points to demand for ingredient-led care for the scalp and beard, focusing on smoothing, repairing, and enhancing shine. #BridalMakeupArtists captures both final results and day-to-day content, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the work and routines of bridal artists. #MillennialSkincare signals continued engagement from this generation, as they share routines that balance efficacy, prevention, and maintenance in skincare. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing aesthetic expression with long-term care and behind-the-scenes visibility across beauty content.

Industry observers note that nail trends are getting personal, with consumers adding letters to their nails or intricate patterns like gingham. Other styles that are popular in search are matcha nails, leaning into soft green tones, influenced by the cultural clout of the beverage. The rise of nail art tools signal growing interest in the techniques behind these looks, as consumers aim to create more complex designs. Together, these trends indicate that the nail category is evolving toward more creative and customizable expression, blending personal style, technique, and design.

According to recent reports, diamond Cosmetics highlights demand for affordable, everyday tools, making essential nail utensils widely accessible. Nail Reformation reflects interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails that offer a salon-level, damage-free alternative to shellac. Kleo Kolor focuses on durable, at-home manicure systems, including gel press-ons and LED gel strips designed for long-lasting wear. The Gel Bottle has released variations of pigments, foils, and brushes that enable the creation of more intricate nail art. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light, while Onyx Professional, with products like Hard As Hoof, points to a preference for treatment-focused nailcare that strengthens and repairs weak or brittle nails.

Industry observers note that on beauty TikTok, #OrangeCandle reflects interest in DIY hacks that show how to make a candle from an orange using simple household items, creating a citrusy aroma. #BlackGirlWashDay highlights routine-focused care tailored to textured hair, emphasizing maintenance and health. #PermRodSetNaturalHair points to technique-driven styling for defined, heat-free curls. #WingedLinerTutorial underscores demand for step-by-step guidance in achieving precise makeup looks, while #LongHairHack signals interest in tips and shortcuts for managing and styling long hair. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking practical, how-to guidance across routines, techniques, and hacks in beauty content.

It has been revealed that current search data reveals a growing interest in functional, personalized makeup. Interest in lip volumizers reflects a demand for hybrid lip products that combine hydration, smoothing, and visible plumping with a high-shine finish. Lipstick printers, associated primarily with YSL, signal curiosity around tech-enabled customization, enabling personalized shades on-demand. Gluten-free lipstick highlights rising awareness of ingredient sensitivities, while medium-coverage concealer points to a preference for balanced, skin-like finishes. Meanwhile, the rise of cool-toned blush underscores a want for precise shade matching, as consumers seek out colors that better complement their undertones. Together, these trends indicate that makeup is evolving toward customized, results-driven routines that combine performance, personalization, and ingredient-conscious choices.

The rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes. Caia Cosmetics highlights a demand for accessible, high-quality makeup that delivers an effortless, glowing look similar to Jung Saem Mool, which leans into a Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Rodan + Fields signals an interest in hybrid complexion products combining coverage with skincare benefits. Overall, makeup is evolving toward accessible, glow-focused, and treatment-infused routines that blend professional performance with everyday wearability.

Recent findings suggest that on TikTok, the rise of #LocDetoxing reflects a demand for deep-cleansing routines that support scalp and hair health, particularly among protective styles. #HairPlop highlights an interest in techniques that enhance natural texture, especially for defining curls with minimal effort. #TakingDownBraids points to maintenance-focused content, as consumers navigate the full lifecycle of protective styles. #SunscreenApplication underscores growing attention to proper usage and technique in daily skincare routines, while #AirbrushSprayTan focuses on in-process guidance, from what to wear to how to ensure even results. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking guidance across application and maintenance in beauty content.

It has been revealed that in skincare, current search data reveals a rising focus on advanced, treatment-led products. Interest in scar sticks reflects demand for targeted solutions that simplify care for specific concerns. PDRN cream and serum signal growing awareness of regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas tied to skin repair and renewal. Exosome serum highlights increasing interest in next-generation, science-backed actives, while high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) underscores the influence of non-invasive, clinic-inspired technologies, as consumers look for lifting and firming benefits beyond topical products. Together, these trends indicate that skincare is evolving toward highly targeted, science-driven routines that blend efficacy, innovation, and treatment-level results.

ELM Biosciences underscores the growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a “lab-to-patient” approach supporting long-term skin health and the concept of aging well. AO Skincare signals demand for antioxidant-rich formulas that strengthen skin resilience against environmental stressors. Organic Apoteke reflects continued interest in holistic, ayurvedic-inspired skincare, as consumers seek gentle solutions for concerns like acne and sensitivity. Yepoda Skincare and Tosowoong, both Korean brands, highlight the influence of active-led formulations and high-concentration products targeting concerns such as acne, pigmentation, and aging.

On TikTok, #MicroLinksHairExtensions are trending, reflecting demand for natural-looking length and volume, as consumers invest in seamless hair enhancements. #ViralDollarTreeMakeup highlights budget-conscious beauty discovery, with users testing affordable products. #HairWashDays points to routine-driven content, as consumers build and share structured care rituals for healthier hair. #PlumperLips underscores ongoing interest in enhancement-focused beauty, whether through techniques or product-driven results, while #MomHairHack spans both child hair solutions and quick, practical styling for moms themselves. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, affordability, and routine-friendly approaches to beauty content.

Sources indicate that current search data reveals a haircare consumer increasingly focused on targeted, treatment-led products. Interest in protein-free shampoo reflects demand for gentler formulations tailored to specific hair needs, particularly for those avoiding protein overload. Amino acid shampoo signals a shift toward ingredient-led repair, as consumers seek formulas that strengthen and support hair health. Dry shampoo paste highlights demand for multi-functional refresh solutions that absorb oil and add texture. Meanwhile, overnight hair serum demonstrates growing interest in treatments that work during sleep, delivering hydration, repair, and frizz reduction without requiring extra time in the morning routine, and red light therapy hats underscore the rising adoption of tech-enabled solutions for scalp health and hair growth. Together, these trends indicate that haircare is evolving toward personalized, treatment-driven routines that combine efficacy, convenience, and innovation.

Playa Beauty reflects interest in California-inspired products promising effortless “beach hair”, supporting minimalist routines while enhancing natural waves and movement. California Baby underscores demand for gentle, plant-based products suitable for babies, children, and adults with sensitive skin. Ducray points to a growing appetite for clinically backed, condition-specific solutions, offering dermatologically tested treatments for dandruff, hair loss, and sensitive scalps. Dr. Groot, a Korean brand, highlights a consumer focus on scalp health and anti-hair loss solutions. Indian-inspired ayurvedic haircare brand Champo uses ingredients such as myrobalan fruit extract, gum arabic, and geranium oil to resonate with a consumer seeking easy packaged haircare, rather than performing weekly ayurvedic hair oiling. California Naturals signals interest in natural, nourishing formulas that strengthen hair.

On TikTok, #DitchedTheDye reflects a shift among older women embracing their natural hair color and moving away from maintenance-heavy routines. #ILoveCurlyHair highlights a growing appreciation for natural texture, as consumers celebrate and care for their curls. #PromMakeupInspo points to planning and inspiration for key events, with owners seeking polished, occasion-ready looks. #CubanTwistHair underscores interest in protective styling and cultural hair practices, while #HairFoam signals demand for styling products that enhance texture and hold. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing self-expression, hair health, and event-driven styling in beauty content.

Industry observers note that consumers are increasingly seeking convenient, easy-to-use formats and wearable solutions for functional wellness, with patches offering targeted support for mood, metabolism and cellular health. Dopamine patches target focus and cognitive performance, while GLP-1 and NAD patches support metabolism, energy and cellular function. Cutting Jelly reflects interest in supplements for weight management and fat reduction and pressotherapy points to growing demand for non-invasive recovery and circulation-boosting treatments. These trends show wellness routines evolving beyond basic supplementation toward a focus on energy to fat reduction and enhanced circulation.

Industry observers note that javvy Coffee reflects growing interest in functional beverages that combine everyday rituals with wellness benefits, offering convenient ways to support energy and focus. A1 Supplements and MTS Nutrition underscore demand for performance-driven sports nutrition, including muscle building, bodybuilding and post-workout recovery, appealing to consumers seeking results-oriented solutions. Lullabites points to a desire for wellness products that support rest and recovery, emphasizing functional snacks designed for relaxation and sleep. IM8 Health, co-founded by David Beckham, highlights interest in simplified, all-in-one nutrition that combines multiple supplements into a single, convenient daily drink. What’s That Patch is delivering patches packed with nutrients that help with sleep, stress, productivity and more. Together, these brands reveal that wellness consumers are seeking products that are functional, evidence-based and seamlessly integrated into daily routines.

Recent findings suggest that #LashGlues highlights interest in product performance and comparison between brands, as consumers test glues for reliable, long-lasting lash applications. #MakeupSamples reflects budget-conscious discovery, with shoppers exploring trial sizes and low-commitment ways to test products. #HairTrial points to planning and preparation, as owners test styles ahead of key moments. Meanwhile, #HerbalHairGrowthOil signals demand for natural, treatment-focused solutions, and #BushyBrows spans interest from managing and shaping fuller brows to enhancing volume and testing products. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, planning and creativity in beauty content.

There’s an increasing focus on functional, treatment-led bodycare products that deliver targeted results. Interest in epsom salt lotions reflects a demand for convenient, topical solutions that soothe sore muscles and support recovery. Searches for kojic acid lotions and turmeric body washes signal a growing focus on brightening and tone correction across the body, as consumers turn to ingredient-led solutions that address hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone. Silicone loofahs and glass foot files point to a preference for hygienic, durable tools that elevate cleansing and exfoliation, while addressing concerns around bacteria and skin safety.

The rise of Crowned Skin reflects a shift toward multifunctional bodycare, as well as an interest in products like body butter colognes, which combine deep hydration with long-lasting fragrance. Bepanthol highlights demand for clinically backed, multi-purpose solutions that protect and regenerate sensitive or compromised skin. Vermont Soap underscores an interest in gentle, non-irritating cleansers and bar soaps that replace harsher detergents, reflecting a move toward safer, skin-friendly formulations. Meanwhile, Luna Daily and Kate McLeod point to growing desire for specialized and ritualized bodycare — from microbiome-balancing formulas safe for all areas of the body, to waterless, solid moisturizers that emphasize sustainability and sensorial experience.

According to recent reports, #CheapBeauty is trending on TikTok, showing that consumers are exploring budget-conscious cosmetic options and highlighting an interest in affordable products. #SkincareComedy reflects engagement with humorous, relatable beauty moments, where audiences enjoy playful takes on everyday experiences. #HairExtensionInstallation points to professional, technique-focused content, as viewers watch skilled stylists demonstrate expert application and installation. Meanwhile, #SkinTighteningTreatment and #VolumeWispy capture aspirational results, from creams that enhance skin firmness to professional lash services that create full, wispy volume, proving that beauty audiences remain captivated by visible, high-impact transformations. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing entertainment, affordability, and aspirational transformations across beauty content.

There’s a craving for gourmand fragrances taking place, as rich, edible-inspired scents capture consumer attention. Searches for masculine fragrances suggest that scent is functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Tomato perfume reflects curiosity around hyper-specific, ingredient-led scents that invite consumers to reimagine familiar smells in a new context. Solid fragrances, meanwhile, point to demand for portable alternatives to spray bottles, where fragrance layering can extend beyond the home. Finally, clean, fresh perfumes reveal how consumers are seeking out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to rich, gourmand notes.

Industry observers note that the popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a consumer shift toward heritage-rich fragrances known for their high-concentration and long-lasting power. YCZ captures the rise of social media-driven accessibility, proving that viral scents can provide high-quality alternatives to designer perfumes at an affordable price point. Narcotica underscores the appeal of the niche Italian market, where the focus is on “addictive”, high-concentration gourmands that blend bold sweetness with luxurious, long-lasting ingredients.

According to recent reports, #TrippyNails are trending, showing that consumers are drawn to surreal, psychedelic nail aesthetics that use distorted patterns and holographic finishes to create eye-catching results. #EasterMakeup reflects a fascination with seasonal, pastel-driven makeup, highlighting how soft color palettes and whimsical details capture attention during spring celebrations. #MakeupCleansingBalm points to growing interest in high-performance cleansers that remove heavy makeup without drying out the skin or leaving it feeling stripped. Meanwhile, #GRWMDate and #HairGoneWrong capture unfiltered, relatable beauty experiences. The former centers on personal storytelling and dating life while getting ready, and the latter highlights the reality of styling mishaps, illustrating how beauty audiences value both the social side of getting ready and the more candid moments that happen along the way.

What’s drawing consumers in? According to data, its playful and creative nail expressions. There’s increased interest in stained glass and matcha nails, as users seek visually striking, color-rich designs that combine artistry with trend-driven aesthetics. Meanwhile, polka dot nails highlight a preference for playful patterns that add personality to everyday manicures. The rise of nail art pens signals a move toward precision and customization. Finally, solid gel nail glue indicates attention to durable, reliable application, showing that consumers value long-lasting performance alongside unique nail looks.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of brands, the rise of Heyhae reflects a shift toward convenient, at-home nail solutions, as more consumers value semi-cured gel strips, which can be applied under natural sunlight for quick, non-toxic manicures. Diamond Cosmetics highlights the demand for affordable, everyday nail tools, making professional-grade manicures accessible to a wide audience. Nail Reformation demonstrates interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails, offering a salon-level, damage-free experience at home. Meanwhile, Sunuv and IBD Beauty underscore the appeal of salon-level equipment and innovations — from UV and LED lamps to builder gel.

Recent findings suggest that this week on TikTok, #RobeCurls are trending, as more consumers are drawn to heatless styling techniques that simplify hair routines while delivering defined, natural-looking results. #IceCreamNails reflects a fascination with playful, dessert-inspired nail aesthetics, which underscore how novelty textures and creative color palettes capture attention across nail content. The #LipOilGloss hashtag spotlights lip products that combine shine, nourishment, and a lightweight feel in everyday routines. Meanwhile, #SoftBridalMakeup and #GenZMakeup captures two parallel beauty directions: one centered on polished, natural elegance for milestone events, and the other revealing side-by-side contrasts between Gen Z and millennial makeup styles. Together, these trends show how consumers are balancing practical beauty solutions, playful visual trends, and cross-generational style influences.

It has been revealed that subtle, natural-looking makeup continues to be popularized by medium-coverage products such as concealers. The rise of cool-toned blush and illuminating drops further signals a move toward color theory-informed customization, where consumers use specific undertones and light-reflecting finishes to create a healthy and natural glow. There’s also demand for clean mascara, where lightweight, ingredient-conscious formulas are favored. Another trend on the rise is gluten-free lipsticks, pointing to growing attention to health-conscious formulations.

The rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Jolie Beauty highlights the demand for alternative, high-performance makeup that allows bold self-expression while remaining vegan and cruelty-free. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes, while Jung Saem Mool underscores the appeal of luxury Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Meanwhile, Concrete Minerals signals a move toward transparent formulations with bold pigments, as shoppers increasingly prioritize ingredient-conscious choices.

According to recent reports, #RushedMakeup highlights that consumers are drawn to quick, ready-to-go routines that demonstrate how to look polished fast. #NailTechASMR reflects fascination with sensory content. #BeforeAndAfterFacelift signals that audiences are intrigued by dramatic visual transformations of cosmetic procedures. #SisterLockRetightening and #WigLaid highlights a strong interest in professional hair care expertise and the maintenance of intricate, high-effort hairstyles, while also capturing attention to precision and seamless style by showcasing how flawlessly wigs are styled and finished.

In a recent development, the rise of scar sticks, PDRN serums, and liquid microneedling reflects a consumer increasingly invested in skin regeneration, barrier repair, and clinically backed ingredients. The portability and ease of scar sticks signal demand for convenient, targeted solutions, while liquid microneedling highlights appetite for professional-level collagen stimulation and enhanced absorption without in-clinic procedures. Growing interest in milk sunscreens signals demand for high-performance UV protection that feels lightweight, skincare-forward, and multifunctional. There’s also growth in matte lip balms, with Celine launching refillable matte lip balms accompanied by a special installation at Harrods on March 2.

According to recent reports, trending skincare brands reflect a shift toward clinically grounded, barrier-focused skin health paired with sustainability and device-led innovation. Genabelle and Tosowoong, both K-beauty brands, exemplify this movement: Genabelle develops science-backed, microbiome and PDRN-driven formulas designed to repair the skin barrier, while Tosowoong targets brightening, anti-aging, acne, and dehydration. At the same time, the growing attention around Shark’s CryoGlow LED mask, targeting acne, fine lines and puffiness, reflects a desire for professional-grade treatments that accelerate results, reduce inflammation, and replicate clinic-grade procedures. Meanwhile, Bolt Beauty’s biodegradable single-dose capsules and Yepoda’s K-beauty-inspired active formulations underscore the rising ingredient literacy of consumers.

Recent findings suggest that on TikTok, the #FlawlessBraids hashtag is largely driven by hair stylists showcasing intricate braiding techniques, alongside AI-generated concepts of futuristic braiding devices that don’t yet exist — but imagine faster styling without sacrificing precision. Meanwhile, #NeonHairColor highlights bold experimentation and personal expression, while #GlowSunscreen reflects a skin-first mindset where protection and radiance are expected to work hand in hand. #ShadowLiner signals interest in detailed, technique-focused eye artistry, as creators break down application methods for more defined eye looks. #LipEssentials points to demand for streamlined, everyday lipcare that balances performance with convenience.

According to recent reports, the surge in beauty tools like red light therapy hats suggests that consumers are increasingly seeing the scalp as the biological foundation of hair quality, density, and longevity, embracing device-led, clinically inspired solutions they can use conveniently at home. Interest in ingredient-specific shampoo formulas featuring batana oil and amino acid, or those that are protein-free, reflects a more educated haircare buyer. Meanwhile, demand for hair smoothing serums points to a parallel desire for immediate polish and manageability. Together, these trends reveal a consumer who approaches haircare through targeted, science-backed and ingredient-conscious solutions.

In a recent development, seapuri and Dr. Groot, both Korean brands, tap into the rising demand for scalp-focused, anti-hair loss care. Seapuri uses hydrating, mineral-rich formulas, including a water-based scalp serum to reduce hair loss and balance sebum, while Dr. Groot focuses on scalp-nourishing shampoos and targeted anti-hair loss solutions with a clinically inspired, results-driven approach. LED brands like CurrentBody, Shark, Solawave, Vym, Monastery and FAQ have also been leading the charge. Roz sits at the intersection of plant-based sustainability and professional performance delivering botanical-powered results that promote lasting scalp health. This positioning bridges the gap between the accessible, plant-based approach of California Naturals and the salon-quality focus of ISO Beauty — underscoring how consumers increasingly seek conscious formulations alongside visible, high-performance results.

Recent findings suggest that on TikTok, hashtags like #BraiderOfTikTok and #BridalGlamLook are largely driven by professionals showcasing intricate techniques and polished transformations, suggesting that owners turn to the platform for inspiration. Meanwhile, #TryingNewHairstyles highlights a culture of experimentation and style switch-ups, while #SkincareMasks documents selfcare routines as part of an ongoing beauty journey. #RedHeadMascara points to growing demand for hyper-specific, shade-inclusive products, revealing that consumers are actively searching for solutions tailored to their unique features.

There’s a growing interest in topical, bioactive wellness formats, with patches incorporating GLP-1s and NAD reflecting a shift to skin-applied solutions for metabolic support, longevity, and targeted physiological optimization. At the same time, consumers are searching for supplements such as oregano oil and L-theanine powder, pointing to continued demand for immune resilience and stress management through more traditional, scientifically informed formats. Cutting jelly, a Korean wellness supplement, is gaining traction for its appetite-suppressing, digestion-supporting, and fat-management proposition. Its popularity highlights a broader preference for convenient, flavorful, and results-driven wellness rituals. Collectively, these trends reflect a consumer mindset that blends experimentation with intentionality, seeking measurable benefits through both topical innovation and functional nutrition.

The latest search trends show that consumers are treating wellness as a seamless part of daily life rather than a task. By brand, Javvy Coffee reflects a desire to turn everyday rituals into functional routines that boost physical performance, while Wellah signals interest in precise, results-driven nutrition for recovery and hydration. Lullabites points to a focus on restorative sleep supporting energy and clarity for the day ahead. Crisp Power highlights the rise of indulgent snacks that also meet fitness goals, and Magic Spoon shows that nostalgic, enjoyable foods are increasingly expected to deliver health benefits without compromising taste.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, hashtags like #PinkAndPurpleHair and #PersonalizedFragrance are driven by owners embracing beauty as a form of self-expression and creativity, from bold hair colors and custom scents to playful hair accessories like bows. Trends such as #LipLinerPencil highlight a desire to explore colors and combinations for defined, polished looks. Meanwhile, content around #RetentionTips indicated that beauty consumers value expert guidance and skillful maintenance, ensuring they get the most out of specialized treatments such as lash extensions.

It has been revealed that consumers are going beyond basic hygiene in search of specialized products, like Epsom salt lotions for muscle recovery. The rising interest in PH-balanced body washes and fungal infection lotions highlights a shift toward dermatological wellness. At the same time, tools like the glass foot file are gaining traction, reflecting a consumer focus on at-home pedicures and skin maintenance. Meanwhile, the demand for Moroccan black soap underscores a desire for ‘heritage efficacy’, where owners seek out natural, ritual-based exfoliation to minimize synthetic chemical alternatives. These trends signal a more literate consumer who views the entire body — not just the face — as a landscape for clinical, preventative, and holistic care.

The rising search interest in brands like GoPure Beauty, QV Skincare, Diptyque, Susanne Kaufmann, and Bliss reflects a consumer shift toward the skinification of the body, whereby customers demand high-performance active ingredients for use beyond their face. This behavior indicates a shift to clinical wellness, with shoppers balancing a need for dermatological efficacy and targeted solutions with a desire for the sensory luxury and ‘clean’ prestige offered by Diptyque and Susanne Kaufmann.

Industry observers note that on TikTok, content featuring hashtags like #HairExtensionInstallation and #BrowThreading are dominated by professionals sharing techniques, as more consumers use the platform to get inspiration or find services. In contrast, #MixedHairstyles and #HairExtensionsHack are mostly driven by people exploring practical options and DIY approaches to at-home styling. Elsewhere, #CrueltyFreeCosmetics reflect a growing interest in ethical and sustainable products, showing that conscious choices are increasingly part of beauty conversations online.

The rise in sweet fragrance searches reveals consumers are craving comfort and indulgence. Interest in tomato perfume and milk fragrances points to a growing appetite for unconventional, nostalgic aromas that blur the line between food and scent. The emergence of edible perfume — designed to be safely consumed — signals a shift toward playful, multisensory experiences in which application extends scent beyond the skin. Meanwhile, demand for white floral perfume suggests that classic, elegant profiles continue to anchor consumer preferences amid experimentation.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a shift toward luxurious and statement-making scents. Assaf, in particular, offers luxurious, often unisex fragrances that combine oud and incense with contemporary, international notes. The rise of Xinu, meanwhile, points to a growing interest in artisanal storytelling and plant-based ingredients. Also on the rise is XO Khloé, underscoring the continued power of celebrity-led fragrance lines.

Industry observers note that the rise of #PinkNailDesign and #BraidsAndBows highlights playful, creative styles, while #GenZMakeup favors fresh-faced, natural looks with fun touches like graphic eyeliner, pastels, and faux freckles. The growth in #JLoMakeup is being driven by Jennifer Lopez’s Golden Globes look, which was inspired by the early-aughts supermodel glam that users are eager to recreate. The growth of #FirstTimeBotox signals increasing openness and transparency around cosmetic procedures, as users frame treatments as relatable milestones rather than taboo transformations. Meanwhile, #HoneyHairMask highlights a parallel interest in plant-based, at‑home haircare rituals focused on nourishment and maintenance.

Consumers are going for self‑expression, playful motifs and hybrid styles when it comes to nail art. Searches for cat eye heart nails, pink cat eye nails, and cat claw nails show that consumers are blending shape‑driven trends with tactile finishes, embracing looks that feel both edgy and whimsical. Meanwhile, strawberry shortcake nails point to a nostalgia‑infused trend. The interest in Cynthia Erivo nails highlights how celebrity‑inspired nail looks can drive demand, with consumers translating red carpet or character‑driven aesthetics into their own manicure repertoire.

Recent findings suggest that the top‑growing nail brands reflect a consumer shift toward at‑home expertise and expressive finishes. Heyhae’s popularity signals a desire for playful, design-forward polishes and tutorials that help users translate looks for everyday wear. Gaoy and Rossi Nails underscore the rise of DIY gel systems and professional‑grade kits, revealing that consumers seek salon‑quality results at home. Jodsone’s ascent points to a craving for art‑centric, niche lacquer brands that stand out with unique color stories. Meanwhile, IBD Beauty highlights continued demand for reliable, performance‑driven products in the professional and enthusiast space, especially among gels and long‑wear finishes.

On TikTok, trending beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that blends identity‑driven aesthetics, routine conservation and sensory‑led selfcare. The popularity of #PastelGothMakeup shows how owners are embracing expressive beauty looks, using makeup as a form of cultural and creative identity. Hashtags like #SkincareRestock and #ShampooRoutine points to the importance of consistency and ritual. #StrawberryScents highlights an interest in nostalgic fragrance profiles, while #BasketballHairstyle reflects the influence of purpose‑driven, activity‑ready beauty content.

Consumers are getting creative thanks to the popularity of peel-off lip tints and liners. The rise of blue lip stain, which applies blue but reveals a pink or berry hue once peeled, speaks to the demand for color-shifting, pH-reactive formulas that feel personalized and surprising. Plumping lip liner reflects a desire for makeup that mimics cosmetic procedures, with consumers drawn to products that visibly enhance lip volume without injections. Meanwhile, plum mascara shows how consumers are exploring non-traditional but wearable color accents.

According to recent reports, the top-growing makeup brands reveal a consumer shift toward inclusive design, minimalist aesthetics, as well as age and tool-specific solutions. Tilt Beauty reflects rising demand for accessible, user-friendly packaging and refillable formats that are sustainable. Sweed Beauty appeals to a growing audience seeking the no-makeup makeup look, through vegan formulations that deliver barely-there finishes for natural enhancement over heavy coverage. Maange shows that consumers are investing in quality makeup brushes and application tools, signaling increased interest in the techniques behind the look, not just the formulas themselves. Meanwhile, Jung Saem Mool attracts those drawn to editorial-inspired, K-beauty artistry, and Prime Prometics caters to the needs of mature skin, emphasizing that makeup shoppers are increasingly seeking products that serve their specific life stage and texture needs.

The rise of #HairExtensionsTutorial and #TakingOutBraids indicates that customers are actively seeking step‑by‑step guidance for maintenance and technique. #FrenchHairPin and #PurpleHairDye underscore a growing appetite for aesthetic experimentation and trend‑inspired looks, where tools and color become playful ways to express personal style. Meanwhile, #UltaHairSalon points to the influence of in‑salon experiences and professional authority in shaping consumer choices, with users looking to bridge DIY learning and expert execution.

Skincare products that blend restorative care, gentle technology and everyday indulgence are on the rise. The popularity of scar sticks and PDRN serums points to the advancement in regenerative treatments that support healing and skin repair. Tools like ultrasonic skin scrubbers highlight consumers’ appetite for at‑home derm‑tech devices. Also, melting lip balms and pore care are trending as consumers seek results‑driven everyday products.

Industry observers note that brands with ingredients-conscious efficacy, modernized wellness and at-home performance solutions are being sought after. Terra Lotus, powered by beef tallow-based care, signals a growing interest in animal-derived, nutrient-dense skincare rooted in traditional practices, as consumers seek richer, bioavailable alternatives to plant oils and lab-created moisturizers.

Sources indicate that APLB and Genabelle continue to spike interest in science-backed K-beauty, especially products targeting hydration, brightening, and skin regeneration through actives like niacinamide and glutathione. Dermagist points to sustained interest in cosmeceutical-style anti-aging solutions. Finally, Shark Beauty’s expansion into skincare devices reflects the growing appeal of tech-enhanced and at-home treatments.

Consumers are eager to participate in viral beauty without overspending, as #AffordableLipOil and #AffordableMascara make strong cases for accessible versions of trendy, functional products. #ProfessionalHairProducts point to a growing appetite for salon-quality care. In contrast, #HydroDermabrasion reflects a rising interest for in-spa skincare treatments, as consumers turn to TikTok to understand the benefits of medical-grade exfoliation and glow-boosting facials. Meanwhile, #CranberryMakeup underscores the continued influence of seasonal and mood-based beauty aesthetics, as customers experiment with rich, warm tones to express personal style.

Exfoliating foot masks and hand masks are on a spike, as consumers approach the treatments with the same ritualistic care traditionally given to the face. Vegan body wash and magnesium body butter reflect a shift toward wellness‑aligned, ingredient‑conscious products. Meanwhile, exfoliating body lotion bridges treatment and care, showing the consumer’s need for multifunctional products that improve texture and moisture in a single step.

In a recent development, kate McLeod and Brown Sugar Babe offer sensory bodycare experiences, from exfoliating stones to whipped butters. Brands like Dettol and Noshinku show that trusted hygiene and germ‑defense solutions remain top of mind. Bend Soap Tech giant’s artisanal approach highlights the appeal of small‑batch, craft formulations.

Recent findings suggest that these top‑growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that values efficacy, personalization, real‑world practicality and community‑driven discovery. The popularity of #ScienceBasedSkincare and #SkincareApp indicates that users are increasingly seeking data‑informed products and digital tools. At the same time, #LazyGirlSkincare and #ThinHairTips reflect a demand for simple, low‑effort solutions that fit into busy lifestyles or specific concerns. On the makeup side, #BlushLovers highlights the enduring appeal of color cosmetics.

The surge in interest for marshmallow perfume and chocolate perfume reflects a continuous craving for gourmand, dessert‑inspired scents. The rise of rose vanilla perfume and bridal perfume suggests people are gravitating toward romantic and memory‑evoking fragrances. Growing searches for oil‑based perfume show an increased interest in long‑lasting and body‑centric scent formats, revealing a preference for fragrance that melds seamlessly with one’s natural scent and lasts longer than traditional sprays.

In a recent development, matière Première takes on the farm‑to‑fragrance purity and minimalist luxury, with its raw material‑focused compositions. La Sultane de Saba Paris channels consumer interest with olfactory-inspired notes. Similarly, The Maker Perfume hints at a growing demand for identity‑driven scent choices over mass market fragrances. Meanwhile, legacy and designer‑adjacent brands like Hugo Boss and Penhaligon’s continue to draw attention for their heritage and status, even as they explore niche alternatives.

Sensitivity-aware routines, personal customization and ingredients‑led problem-solving beauty are growing hashtags on TikTok.

Sources indicate that the popularity of #SensitiveSkincare shows more people are seeking gentle, irritation‑free formulas. Meanwhile, #UnderratedSkincare suggests a hunger for hidden gems or under-the-radar products, meaning consumers are increasingly willing to explore beyond mainstream brands. The rise of #BlondeHighlightsOnDarkHair and #HairLoss captures demand for hair‑specific solutions and transformation content, as users look for guidance and community advice on challenging hair goals. Finally, #CoffeeSkincare points to the ongoing appeal of natural, functional ingredients, as people are drawn to the antioxidant and circulation‑boosting benefits of coffee in skin and hair routines.

In a recent development, bold nails are back and it’s all about self‑expression and textured innovation with growing interest in statement cheetah print designs rooted in nostalgia and glamour, blending animal prints with modern finishes and clever color shifts. The appetite for animalistic styles continues with cat eye nails reflecting excitement around method‑driven finishes — using magnetic polish to create shimmering dimension that feels both futuristic and accessible. Water drop nails and junk nails are also making noise with sleek, sculptural texture for the former and a maximalist approach to the latter with oversized charms, clashing textures and extreme customization.

Sources indicate that consumers are leaning into at-home expertise and expressive finishes. Gaoy and MelodySusie highlight a growing investment in DIY tools like gel kits, lamps and drills. Nail Labo caters to a rising demand for precision and minimalist artistry, drawing from Japanese nail culture that prioritizes clean lines, quality materials and technical skill. Caudalie introduces a skincare-forward angle with its hand and nailcare rooted in antioxidant-rich formulations. Meanwhile, Ethereal Lacquer is capturing attention through its holographic, metallic and multi-chrome polishes, signaling that many nail consumers are seeking and collecting bold, light-catching finishes that double as artistic self-expression.

The popularity of #OilToFoamCleanser reflects growing interest in innovative hybrid formats, suggesting consumers are drawn to easy and elevated routines. #OilySkinHack points to a problem-solving mindset, where users seek shareable solutions tailored to specific skin concerns, especially shine and congestion. Meanwhile, #ManiInspo and #GlitterHighlighter showcase visual beauty through inspiration and self-expression, with consumers looking for aesthetic ideas that feel fresh, playful and mood-driven. Lastly, #EdgeControlFor4cHair emphasizes the demand for texture-specific solutions and culturally resonant beauty techniques.

Matte powder is trending, as consumers seek polished, smooth and filtered‑like skin finishes. The popularity of pink lip stain and lipstick pencil, meanwhile, highlights a tilt toward bold lip looks that are still accessible and day‑to‑day friendly. Techniques like tightline eyeliner illustrate how subtle definition is gaining traction, reflecting a preference for minimal effort with big impact. Contrastingly, the surge in black lip stains suggest that consumers are also embracing more daring, identity‑driven looks that go beyond enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that among the top‑growing makeup brands, there’s an emphasis on accessible, niche aesthetics and cultural authenticity across price points. BBIA’s K‑beauty roots and affordable, vibrant product lines show how makeup lovers are drawn to colorful products that promote self-expression. Kulfi Beauty’s South Asian-inspired, inclusive shade range underscores a demand for brands that acknowledge and celebrate underrepresented skin tones and identities. On the other end of the pricing spectrum, Hermès brings luxury craftsmanship and premium finishes to makeup, signaling that consumers also view beauty as a status and lifestyle experience. Meanwhile, Palladio Beauty and UCoolMe illustrate how ingredient-driven products and purpose‑driven formats (like lash clusters) are becoming non‑negotiable for many buyers.

On beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer behavior shift toward accessibility, self‑expression and targeted problem‑solving. The surge in #EyelashLiftAndTint showcases how owners are seeking out tutorial‑friendly content and at‑home techniques to achieve salon‑level transformations. Meanwhile, #BraidingExtensions and #NailsDesignIdeas point to a growing appetite for creative styling and personalization in hair and nails. At the same time, #KojicAndTurmericSoap highlights the fascination with viral, ingredient‑centric skincare that promises visible pay-off through ‘miracle’ formulas. Lastly, #PinkLipLiner reflects a subtle shift from cool-tone nudes toward warmer, reddish-pink tones that add soft color while still feeling natural — indicating consumers’ evolving preference for makeup that enhances without overpowering.

The rise of morning shed, the ritualized removal of multiple overnight beauty tools and treatments, highlights a growing fascination with stacked, intensive skincare routines that promise overnight results. Searches for face-lifting masks reflect a desire for visible tightening, while hydrogel’s jelly-like, cooling texture satisfies a craving for sensorial, soothing formats. Meanwhile, rising interest in milky toners and turmeric face creams shows demand for gentle nourishment and targeted actives, with turmeric specifically valued for its natural, hyperpigmentation-reducing benefits.

In a recent development, by brand, Grace & Stella and Byoma each represent a demand for approachable, feel-good skincare — whether through playful formats like eye masks or barrier-repair formulas that emphasize maintenance and simplicity. In contrast, brands like AnteAge, Bioeffect and Medik8 cater to a results-focused audience seeking science-led actives like EGF and retinal, signaling rising trust in clinical, regenerative skincare that targets aging and skin renewal at a deeper level. Consumers are embracing a dual approach to skincare, blending routine-friendly support with targeted, high-performance treatments, depending on need, mood, or life stage.

In the TikTok sphere, trending beauty hashtags are focusing on age inclusivity, professional-level prep, and tailored care for specific identities and beauty concerns. #BeautyOver60 spotlights content that speaks directly to mature audiences, as those aged 60-plus seek routines and products that speak to their evolving needs and celebrate aging confidently. #BridalSkinPrep, often used by makeup artists, reflects interest in expert-driven techniques that enhance makeup application, as consumers value the behind-the-scenes steps that create flawless, event-ready skin. Meanwhile, #CollegeHairstylist, #RedHaircare and #CeramideSerum point to highly specialized content — from on-campus hairstyling services to color-specific hair routines and barrier-supporting ingredients — illustrating a broader trend toward community-rooted expertise and ingredient-conscious skincare.

Haircare is of increasing importance to consumers, as beauty focuses go beyond the surface to tackle cosmetic concerns at their root. The rise of DHT blocker shampoos and scalp serums signal growing concern around hair thinning and scalp health, with consumers turning to targeted treatments that address hair loss at its source. Interest in lightweight conditioners and hair UV protection highlights desire for gentle hydration and environmental defense, which avoids build-up and leans into skincare. Hair fiber powders are also rising, especially among young males, as consumers seek quick-fix solutions to thinning and receding, concerns becoming more prevalent in social dialogue.

According to recent reports, among haircare brands, there’s a consumer shift toward precision and wellness‑infused formulations. Cerave’s expansion into haircare underscores the demand for dermatologist‑approved, barrier‑support solutions — with ceramides and niacinamide anchoring formulas that consider scalp health as closely tied to hair health. Arey taps into a preventative and repigmentation‑focused niche by offering clinical systems to address greying hair, as more consumers seek anti‑aging hair solutions. Design Essentials and TGIN highlight a growing emphasis on texture‑specific haircare, delivering salon‑quality formulas for relaxed, natural and coily hair types. Meanwhile, Vichy brings its skin‑science heritage to hair with targeted treatments for dandruff.
